purpose: A learned codec separates transformation and coding
introduction: An autoencoder with eight latent numbers has eight coordinates, not a declared eight-bit message. Trace the operations that turn one latent coefficient into transmitted bits and a reconstruction.
geometry: Trace a named coefficient through analysis transform y, round to q, probability mass model Q(q), entropy coder to actual bits, entropy decoder, and synthesis to Xhat. Draw a separate training-only branch adding uniform noise to y and taking a differentiable expectation proxy; it reconnects to the objective, not to the actual bitstream.
interpretation: An analysis transform maps the source to real-valued latents y. Quantization maps y to discrete indices q. A probability model supplies masses for those indices; a lossless entropy coder converts them to bits. The receiver uses the agreed model and syntax to recover indices, then a synthesis transform produces X̂. Each arrow performs a different job. An entropy model does not itself reconstruct the image, and a synthesis transform does not specify how its inputs were transmitted.
checks: Distortion changes the reconstruction; entropy coding is lossless for quantized symbols under the declared model. A training noise sample is not a transmitted integer or an observed bit count.
